title: Join Us
text:
We welcome expressions of interest from people excited about computational pathology, cancer biology, artificial intelligence, and spatial omics.
Our work sits at the intersection of methods and biology. Experience in image analysis, machine learning, bioinformatics, or cancer research is relevant, along with curiosity and a willingness to learn across disciplines.

title: Join Us
text:
How to express interest
Please prepare a brief description of your research interests, a CV, and links to relevant publications or projects. Explain how your interests connect with the lab’s research.

Recruitment details to be confirmed: specific openings, eligibility and application routes, start dates, and the lab’s University of Utah contact email. This page invites expressions of interest and does not yet list confirmed vacancies.

title: Research
text: We connect tissue structure, cellular neighborhoods, and molecular measurements to understand cancer, primarily focusing on three themes: (1) AI model development for large-scale pathology image analysis, (2) Multi-modal integration, including radiology, pathology and omics data, and (3) pollutant’s effect on tumor microenvironment in lung cancer for never-smokers.

title: Research
section: AI model development for large-scale pathology image analysis
text:
AI model development for large-scale pathology image analysis
How can routine tissue images reveal meaningful differences in cancer? We develop interpretable image analysis methods to characterize cells, tissue architecture, and tumor heterogeneity, with an emphasis on biological understanding and clinical relevance.



Conceptual workflow from tissue images through cell and tissue analysis to biological interpretation.

title: Research
section: Multi-modal integration, including radiology, pathology and omics data
text:
Multi-modal integration, including radiology, pathology and omics data
Cancer develops within a complex community of tumor, immune, and stromal cells. We investigate how their arrangement and interactions relate to disease progression and treatment response. 



Conceptual workflow from tissue images through cell and tissue analysis to biological interpretation.

Huntsman Cancer Institute
Department of Oncological Sciences
University of Utah





I am an Assistant Professor in the Department of Oncological Sciences and Huntsman Cancer Institute at the University of Utah. My research program develops computational approaches using artificial intelligence (AI) that transform routinely collected pathology specimens into quantitative representations of tumor biology and integrates these features with omics and clinical data to answer clinically and biologically meaningful questions.
Prior to joining the U, I was working as an Instructor and then a principal data scientist in the lab led by Dr. Yinyin Yuan at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center (2023 to 2026). My postdoc trainined was completed in Dr. Yuan’s lab at the Institute of Cancer Research (ICR), UK (2020 to 2023), and I received my Ph.D. in Optics, Photonics and Image Processing at Ecole Centrale Marseille, France (2016 to 2019).
I am actively looking for talented students and postdocs as the founding members for Pan Lab! See how to join the lab.
